name: L'Umbracle
key_features: Calatrava's sculpture garden and landscaped walk in Valencia's City of Arts and Sciences, planted with native species.

name: Steiner House
key_features: Considered one of the major works of Adolf Loos, in Vienna.

name: Aschanska Villa
key_features: A listed Umeå villa by Ragnar Östberg, completed in 1906 for a colonel and now a restaurant.

name: Banovina Palace (Novi Sad)
key_features: A 1936-40 Novi Sad government complex by Dragiša Brašovan, mixing modernism with art deco.

name: Copenhagen City Hall
key_features: The Danish National Romantic city hall by Martin Nyrop, built 1892 to 1905 in Renaissance Revival style.

name: Campus Einaudi
key_features: A Turin university campus on Lungo Dora Siena, named after Italy's second president, Luigi Einaudi.

name: Dia Beacon
by: Robert Irwin, Alan Koch, Lyn Rice, Galia Solomonoff, Linda Taalman
key_features: A former Nabisco box-printing factory near the Hudson, renovated for Dia's art collection with Robert Irwin and OpenOffice architects.

name: Bellevue Arts Museum
key_features: Steven Holl's three-story 2001 building across from Bellevue Square; the museum closed in 2024.

name: 66 Old Church Street, Chelsea
key_features: Gropius and Fry's house for the politician and playwright Benn Levy, part of a joint scheme with Cohen House.

name: Alfa Palace
key_features: A functionalist building by Bohuslav Fuchs, with an inner arcade linking two streets and a square.

name: Carew Tower
key_features: A 49-storey Art Deco skyscraper in Cincinnati, the city's tallest building from 1930 until 2011.

name: Dortmund City and State Library
key_features: Mario Botta's central library, opposite Dortmund's main station; moved in May 1999.

name: Cine Brasília
key_features: Oscar Niemeyer's cinema in Brasília, opened on 22 April 1960 during the new capital's inauguration.

name: Vestersøhus
key_features: A seven-storey red-brick block by Kay Fisker and C. F. Møller, a key work of Danish functionalism, completed 1939.

name: Adria Palace
key_features: A cubist monument in Prague's New Town, facing the ARA palace.

name: Langham House Close
key_features: Stirling and Gowan's first major joint project: three Grade II* listed blocks, influenced by Le Corbusier.

name: Dům Radost
key_features: A 52 m functionalist tower with a cruciform plan inspired by Le Corbusier, once the country's tallest office building.

name: Case Study House No. 1
key_features: A single-story house in the Case Study Houses program, completed in 1948 with glass, concrete block and plywood.

name: Fine Arts Center (Massachusetts)
key_features: Kevin Roche's 646-foot-long bridge of studio art space, raised 30 feet off the ground as a campus gateway.

name: Casa Cattaneo
key_features: Cesare Cattaneo's best-known rationalist building, a 1938–39 rental house in Cernobbio, designed without client constraints.

name: Palace of Assembly
key_features: A parliament built for the Punjab sun: portico, brise-soleil and a hyperboloid chamber.

name: National Congress of Brazil
key_features: Twin office towers rise between an upturned bowl and a dome set on a long flat roof deck.

name: Casa Milà
key_features: Undulating stone facade on columns, two light courts and a catenary-arched attic.

name: National September 11 Memorial
key_features: Two square voids on the tower footprints with water falling into a further central drop.

name: Secretariat Building
key_features: Long concrete slab with a brise-soleil grid, a roof terrace and sculptural ramp towers.

name: Casa Batlló
key_features: Bone-like facade and a light well tiled from deep to pale blue to even out the daylight.

name: Royal Festival Hall
key_features: Egg in a box: the auditorium is raised above open foyers that flow beneath it.

name: Wotruba Church
key_features: 152 concrete blocks stacked irregularly, with glazing filling the gaps between them.

name: Chapel of St. Ignatius
key_features: Tilt-up concrete box under curved roof lanterns, each with coloured lenses and baffles for a liturgy.

name: Church on the Water
key_features: A glass wall slides fully open onto a shallow pool holding a steel cross against the forest.

name: Borobudur
key_features: A stone stupa-mountain of square terraces and round platforms, climbed along carved clockwise galleries.

name: Butaro District Hospital
key_features: Local volcanic stone walls, cross-ventilated wards and outdoor waiting areas reduce airborne infection.

name: 56 Leonard Street
key_features: Floor plates shift and cantilever so each flat gets its own outline and terraces.

name: Esplanade - Theatres on the Bay
key_features: Two glazed shells wrapped in triangular aluminium sunshades that filter tropical light.

name: Casa das Histórias Paula Rego
key_features: Red concrete volumes with two pyramidal towers that bring light into galleries set among trees.

name: Wohnpark Alt-Erlaa
key_features: Stepped slabs with planted terraces on the lower floors and rooftop swimming pools for all residents.

name: Steilneset Memorial
key_features: A silk-membrane corridor hung in a long timber frame, with one window and bulb for each victim.

name: Bridge of Peace
key_features: Pedestrian steel bridge under a wave-shaped glass canopy fitted with LEDs, crossing the Kura river.

name: London Eye
key_features: Cantilevered observation wheel held by an A-frame and cables, its rim spoked like a bicycle wheel.

name: Basilica of the Annunciation
key_features: A two-level church over the excavated grotto, crowned by a lantern dome shaped like an inverted lily.

name: Hungarian Parliament Building
key_features: Symmetrical Gothic Revival riverfront range around a central domed hall.

name: Australian War Memorial
key_features: Cloistered courtyard and pool lead on axis to a domed Hall of Memory lined in mosaic.

name: Napier Museum
key_features: Kerala gabled roofs and polychrome brick walls adapted for natural ventilation of the halls.

name: Gehry Residence
key_features: A pink 1920s bungalow wrapped in corrugated metal, chain-link and tilted glass cubes.

name: Casa Calvet
key_features: Symmetrical stone front with curving gables and wrought-iron balconies, Gaudí's most restrained work.

name: Dresden Central Station
by: Ernst Giese and Paul Weidner; roof by Foster + Partners
key_features: Iron train-shed vaults re-covered with a translucent fabric membrane that lets daylight through.

name: Matthäuskirche Pforzheim
key_features: Walls of a concrete honeycomb grid infilled with coloured glass blocks fill the church with tinted light.

name: Co-Cathedral of the Great Mother of God (Gran Madre di Dio)
key_features: A pierced, sail-like white screen rises above the church and is reflected in pools below.

name: Robert C. Weaver Federal Building
key_features: Curved X-shaped plan raised on sculpted concrete pilotis, its precast window grid repeated on every face.

name: Agora Theatre
key_features: A faceted, folded skin of orange and yellow panels wraps the stage tower and foyers.

name: Diözesanmuseum Paderborn
key_features: Lead-clad block beside the cathedral, holding one tall hall of stepped gallery platforms.

name: Centre de Cultura Contemporània de Barcelona (CCCB)
key_features: A glass wall folds out over an old courtyard, mirroring views across the city to those standing below.

name: Messe Torhaus
key_features: An office block split in two and joined at the top, forming a gate over the tracks into the fair.

name: Bodegas Güell
key_features: A steep stone wedge of a winery on the Garraf coast, with parabolic arches and a chapel under the roof.

name: Qatar National Convention Centre
key_features: Two branching steel 'sidra trees' carry the long canopy across the glass entrance front.

name: Hospicio Cabañas
key_features: Neoclassical hospice of many courtyards, its chapel dome painted with Orozco's murals.

name: Ananda Temple
key_features: Cross-plan brick temple; high hidden openings light four standing Buddhas from above.

name: Alisher Navoi Opera and Ballet Theatre
key_features: A Soviet classical opera house whose side foyers were each carved in ganch by craftsmen of a different region.

name: ECLAC Building
key_features: Raised square ring of concrete offices around a courtyard, beside a spiral ramp and a conical council chamber.

name: Neviges Pilgrimage Church
key_features: Folded concrete roof like a rock mass over a cave-like nave lit by red stained glass.

name: Villa Méditerranée
key_features: Its upper floor cantilevers 40 m over a pool of sea water, with a conference hall sunk below it.

name: House in Cap Ferret
key_features: Raised on twelve micro-piles among the pines; the trees pass straight through the house in flexible sleeves.

name: Aspire Tower (The Torch Doha)
key_features: A 300 m concrete core with floors cantilevered off it, wrapped in steel mesh and topped by a lattice torch.

name: British Council, New Delhi
key_features: An axis through layered courts; Howard Hodgkin's banyan tree in black and white stone spans the facade.

name: Dispensario Antituberculoso
by: Josep Lluís Sert, Josep Torres Clavé, Joan Baptista Subirana (GATCPAC)
key_features: GATCPAC's rationalist tuberculosis clinic in Barcelona's Raval, by Sert, Torres Clavé and Subirana.

name: Apollo Pavilion
key_features: Walk-through sculpture of white in-situ concrete planes bridging a small lake in a new town; Grade II*.

name: Dornbusch Church
key_features: 1960s church partly torn down and closed by a new wall keeping imprints of the old; its footprint is marked outside.

name: Institute of Education
key_features: Long concrete-and-glass block on a raised podium, with tall service towers and stepped ends; only part was built.

name: Alila Villas Uluwatu
key_features: Clifftop resort of low terraced villas and open lattice pavilions, built with local stone and reclaimed timber.

name: Shoto Museum of Art
key_features: Curved wall of rough Korean granite under a bronze-louvred eave; galleries round a deep light well with fountains.

name: Leeza SOHO
key_features: Glass tower split by a 194 m atrium that twists 45 degrees up its height, the world's tallest.

name: Beijing Daxing International Airport Terminal
key_features: Starfish plan: six curved piers radiate from a central hub, among the world's largest single terminals.

name: Stuttgart City Library (Stadtbibliothek am Mailänder Platz)
key_features: Cube with a 9x9 glass-block facade; inside, a skylit four-storey 'heart' and a funnel-shaped hall ringed by books.

name: University of Deusto Library
key_features: Compact library block with chamfered corners, wrapped in glass behind a fine metal screen.

name: Blues Point Tower
key_features: Lone 24-storey tower of 144 flats, meant as the forerunner of high-density housing on McMahons Point.

name: Dorset Street Flats
key_features: Eight small flats with courtyards in load-bearing concrete block; a founding work of the Christchurch School.

name: Adam Art Gallery Te Pātaka Toi
key_features: University gallery squeezed between three older buildings over an abandoned 1960s stair, entered via a glass box.

name: 1 Bligh Street
key_features: Oval 30-storey office tower with Australia's first full double-skin glass facade around a tall naturally lit atrium.

name: Centro per l'arte contemporanea Luigi Pecci
key_features: 1988 museum with a 2016 U-shaped extension adding 3,000 m2 of galleries and an 800-seat amphitheatre.

name: Dudley Zoo
by: Berthold Lubetkin and Tecton (engineer Ove Arup)
key_features: Pre-stressed reinforced concrete gave curved structures and projecting platforms; cages avoided.

name: St David's Hall
key_features: Called complex late brutalism by Building Design, with open foyers.

name: Cyncoed Methodist Church
key_features: International Modern church of rectilinear glass and buff-coloured brick.

name: Converse Memorial Library
key_features: Richardson library that housed the Malden Public Library from 1885 to 1996.

name: Cinerama Dome
by: Pierre Cabrol and Welton Becket & Associates
key_features: Only concrete geodesic dome in the world, built from 316 hexagonal and pentagonal pieces.

name: Benaroya Hall
key_features: Performance hall rests on rubber pads isolating it from the outer shell.

name: Toronto Reference Library
key_features: Canada's largest public reference library, opened in 1977 as the Metropolitan Toronto Reference Library.

name: Cinquantenaire Arcade
key_features: Triple arch topped by a bronze quadriga; Girault replaced Bordiau's single arch but kept his quadriga.

name: CEC Palace
key_features: Eclectic bank headquarters topped by a glass and metal dome; designed by Gottereau, built 1897–1900.

name: Administrative Palace, Satu Mare
key_features: Brutalist administrative palace built 1972–84 by Nicolae Porumbescu, assisted by Ludovic Gyüre.

name: Haludovo Palace Hotel
key_features: A 'hotel city': varied building types spread through existing vegetation and linked by walkways; 1969–72.

name: Sofia Central Station
key_features: New terminal by Transproekt under Milko Bechev beside the 1888 station; inaugurated 6 September 1974.

name: Kuala Lumpur Railway Station
key_features: Indo-Saracenic mix of Western and Mughal styling: horseshoe and ogee arches and large corner chhatris.

name: Caferağa Medrese
key_features: Gate leads to an inner courtyard around which the learning rooms stand.

name: Ben Gurion Airport Terminal 3
key_features: Terminal 3 has 40 gates on four concourses; vertical surfaces are clad in Jerusalem stone.

name: Bab Al Bahrain
key_features: Large central arch over a road, the entrance to Manama souq, flanked by two pedestrian arches.

name: Deira Clocktower
key_features: Clock tower built in 1965 as a symbol of Dubai, at a roundabout where major routes met.

name: Moscow Cinema
key_features: Theatre opened 12 December 1936; 1983 facade shows scenes from Soviet-Armenian films.

name: Tbilisi City Assembly Building
key_features: Neo-Moorish 'Exotic' style from the 1878 remodel; clock tower added 1910.

name: Basílica del Salvador
key_features: Neo-Gothic brick basilica, designed by Teodoro Burchard and completed in 1932; damaged in 1985 and 2010.

name: Cusco Cathedral
by: Juan Miguel de Veramendi, Juan Correa, Miguel Gutiérrez Sencio, Francisco Becerra
key_features: Main temple of Cusco and seat of its archdiocese, completed 1654.
